I played Alien Isolation and liked it very much.
I thought when buying a more recent game, that the quality of the interface would be much better ... bad luck. It felt that I was not going 8 years further in time but 8 and more years  back.

It's a great game. But you shouldn't get THIS version, the one you want is the Super Turbo Championship Edition, which is the same game but expanded with more levels and an extra powerup. I have no idea why they are for sale separately instead of as DLC. Don't buy this, get the better version, also on Steam!

This games horror is so good, The game doesn't seem too scary at first, goofing around with your friends and saying stupid ♥♥♥♥. Its all fun in games until your friends die, what seemed like laughter and yap of the 4 members of your team has quickly turned into just silence. Since every creature in this game can roam around freely around the endless maze of the building, you have that danger of running into anything. you could run into the bracken, jester, bunker spider, hoarding bug, thumper, or the little girl, oh man the little girl...  And while you freak out alone, your friends can laugh at you while spectating you

Updated Review: 

This game was good when EA dropped, it is nearing great now. The art style is incredibly cool, the story is engaging, and the world itself is just awesome to explore. The combat is difficult to start, but satisfying to learn, and has a lot of range to it with all of the different weapon types. Exploration is worthwhile and the interconnected-ness of the world reminds me of dark souls 1. 

Just get it, you'll dig it.

I’m not even a horror fan, but Silent Hill 2 might be one of the best games I’ve ever played.

This game forces you to stay with it. The atmosphere is oppressive, the sound design is incredible, and the story is easily one of the best I’ve seen in gaming. It’s psychological, disturbing, and sticks with you long after you stop playing.

It’s not perfect — PC optimization can be rough and the combat feels clunky at times — but honestly, the story and atmosphere completely make up for it.

I got the In Water ending on my first playthrough, which hit hard and made me want to replay the game in the future to experience the other endings.

An unforgettable experience.
9/10

I have had a blast playing this game. The controls are tight and very responsive. I never felt like I was taking damage when I shouldn't have. The bosses played (so far) have been tough but fair. There was only one part where I got stuck and didn't know where to go for a fair bit of time. Once you get past that one part, the map opens up and you can go just about anywhere and make progress. 

Highly recommended.

Honestly didn’t expect much from this. Thought it was just another flashy Soulslike that looks good in trailers and plays mid. But man… I was wrong.

A few hours in and I’m completely hooked. The combat is super tight, the atmosphere pulls you in, and the boss fights? Absolute bangers. I’ve played Elden Ring, God of War, all that and this holds up. Maybe even better in some ways.

You can tell the devs poured everything into it. The way they showcase their mythology, the world-building, the details… it’s not just a game, it’s a love letter to their culture.

As I said , didn’t expect much, but it ended up being something special. You can feel the heart behind it.

Incredibly disappointing.

Every single thing that's been connected to the previous games, such as; keep calm or critical qte's premenissions and so forth has been replaced by overly used stealth sequenses, extremely long cut scenes and inconsistent writing.

Expected a much better game since it's been delayed and not locked to a strict deadline.

Amazing game. The art style looks awesome, super stylish and unique. The story had me hooked all the way through, and even the side quests were fun and interesting

The main bosses are all different and really fun to fight. Each one felt fresh and stood out in a good way. I had a great time from start to finish

 10/10

So i just got this game yesterday, along with the original (Because it was a bundle) and on my Dell Laptop, and i say it works fine, it looks great and the game hasn't crashed yet. The only negative things i can say about this are:
- Why do we need both Bioshock and Bioshock Remastered? Makes no sense.
- Enemies glitch out sometimes, Ex: A Leadhead Splicer had his head kept rapidly moving up and down while running away.
- Some textures didn't load in all of the way, Ex: the statue in the beginning with Andrew Ryan's head on it and the face didn't load all the way in and it looked like he was wearing a rubber mask. It's the same with all of the other statues too.
Everything else looks amazing and overall so far the game is pleasurable and very atmospheric, i reccomend it to all.
As a South Park fan, I can't praise this masterpiece enough. The best South Park game ever. love it.

Playing this on an RTX 5070 TI and have 0 issues so far.

my only complaint is that it is too short. have more cases for the duck detective to solve please! he needs the money to afford that sweet sweet bread.

This game seems weirdly insistent on sabotaging its own fun. The challenges range from free to grindy, some shoes just absolutely stomp on balance, and being able to just skip encounters by just rushing to the next room can really make you miss some good stuff.
I actually think you'll have the most fun by not wearing any shoes, dont bother with challenges, and go for max kills per stage. At that point you'll have a reasonably good time through the impressively varied encounters and comedic moments, if a bit short with how you'll likely be blazing through the game without those.
The game does have some jank to it, but again the variety of everything involved helps mitigate that a lot. I can easily recommend this as long as you take what ive said in mind and know the type of game you're getting into.
love the game but the community is unbearable.
this game is easily one of my favorites from the year, it's insane, stuff can just occur and the game refuses to elaborate in the most unapologetically dismissive way

Two hours into Prey and I'm already terrified of everything.

Whacking at everything with wrenches to make sure they're not Mimics, turn around and scream at a chair that's behind me. Hit it wildly. Ordinary chair. I relax. The coffee cup next to it attacks me, I whack it out of reflex and start to laugh. 

Then my bedside lamp flickered and I smashed it against a wall.

Good times. Good times.

10/10 would suspect my furniture to be Mimics again.

The visuals are stunning woth plenty of Easter eggs.

The story is standard, but enjoyable enough.

I didn't think gameplay would be as linear as it is though - think still wakes the deep.

Overall a fun diversion that shows promise for things to come, it will be interesting to see future games once some aspects are polished up.

The perfect example that games don't always have to be challenging to be good.
One of the most memorable games I've ever played! Stunning visuals, lovely world, awesome bossfights and the music just hits different. Play it. NOW!

This game expressed every complicated emotions I went through after losing my mother, it conveyed without any dialogues but with music and art.
 I'm now struggling with the last stage of grief.Somewhere in the game when I reached to the grave, without any background knowledge, I felt like I had to sing and I burst into crying. 
When I opened my eyes I saw "acceptance" achievement!
As if someone hugged me and said "I truly understand you".

This is a short and simple indie game that really expands on the interactive game genre. Aesthetically, the designs are simplistic and sufficiently detailed to enhance the ambience of the game. At the  affordable sale price of $0.49, there isn't really much of an opportunity for any nitpicking. Briefly summarising, the game places you in the shoes of a man plotting for a murder, striving to get away scot-free. With a vast range of options and various approaches you can take, the game flaunts its versatility and variety of game-ending outcomes. Honestly, if you're looking for a quick, cheap game for your entertainment, consider "The Deed".

Great game, smashing enemies is even more fun than in the first game and traversal is excellent. Although you don't get as attached to the bad guys minions as in the first game and i think a dlc that doesn't add story content shouldn't add achievements it still a very fun time.

I can highly recommend Dredge to any one who suffers from gamer apathy or has trouble getting hooked in by games. Though simple the core game play loop is fun an interactive, while the story pulls the player in to the eldritch mystery that actually makes you have to problem solve more for the story then any of the game play challenges/mechanics. Overall only complaint is there is not more Dredge to be played after finishing the game.
The game is basically robots, smurfs, and humans being given immortality by a giant ping pong ball in order to fight the forces of evil geometry.

Good game. I bought it looking for a relatively mindless, easy shooter and this satisfied that itch pretty well. The story was decently engaging too, with lots of references and funny moments -  like a guy staring at an abstract painting going "do you think they hung it upside down?"

 There are a few different areas and a reused, small open-world area where you can "serve and protect" with side missions. It did crash several times with random "fatal errors", but the auto save is frequent enough to where it wasn't a major issue. It's fairly short, about 8-10hrs, so I'd say get it on sale.

Fun game when you have the momentum going, but it suffers from the serious case of not having an identity
It has an obscene amount of mini games, and often you are forced to play those if you want to unlock more upgrades for your character. No pay to win (for the most part) is nice, though at the same time all the good cosmetics are locked behind the gacha paywall with the hard pity mechanic.
Progression is constantly halted by an upper limit of things, either resets daily or resets weekly, and often the rewards are also locked behind quests.

at the end of the day, it feels like I am playing for a 2nd job than a game outside of the story mode. Fun if you are playing the story mode, other than that it's pretty shallow all around.

Pretty fun game!
Minor bugs though. 
If I get hit by an enemy while I was in the process of putting my sword into the purple high jump block, even at my last bar of life, I’m still alive. I was walking around with zero life bar. lol.

This is a masterclass in Metroidvania game design.
There aren’t many truly original ideas here, but everything is executed to perfection.
Highly recommended!

Great combo of the action packed RE4 story and the mystery and horror of RE7.
This game was a certified banger

buy on sale and enjoy the story, Ea being the evil corporation it is abandoned the game shortly after it released and truly left what could have been a gem in the dustbin of gaming history. As a star wars fan this game is worth it for the ability to fly a x wing and a tie interceptor in vr with immersive combat and a really good singe player campaign.

How to Fish’s such a sick multiplayer party banger. The fact that online runs perfectly even with no accelerator on regular home internet already puts it head and shoulders above most similar games. Never dropped once for me, server stability’s totally solid.
Tons of clever little touches in the weapons, skins n inspect animations too. Nothing totally game changing or anything, but they all bump up the whole experience real nice. And let’s not sleep on how insane the sniper teamkill feedback feels. Once everyone’s rocking a sniper, the whole game’s vibe flips completely. Straight up hands all the fun right back to the players. If the devs keep cranking out updates n drop workshop support later down the line, this game’s 100% gonna be the next huge viral smash.
Lazy Mattman got me into this game, and it is absolutely great

A great successor that's worth playing. I enjoyed every minute and it's also easy to get all achievements.

The game offers different difficulties that you can easily change for a save slot.

It runs very well on the Steam Deck and you can easily get 3-4h of battery life. It's worth mentioning that every time I closed the game, the Deck restarted. That's not a big issue, just a bit inconvenient.

This is the most well made "difficult" game I've ever played. The game is brutal in its difficulty, but all of your deaths are caused by you. The game never throws any bulls**t deaths at you and there's no forced backtracking to retrieve lost items from death (because there are no items). When you die, there's no game over screen and loading. You're just immediately back without even a second of delay. The developers were keenly aware of how difficult the game they were making was and made it an extremely enjoyable experience. This game is a masterclass in platforming game design. I highly recommend this to anyone who wants to put their platforming skills to the test.

The game is pretty bad, not even the style can save it. The strongest part of the game — namely, the visual presentation — is not flawless: misaligned models here and there and poor camera management in some scenes, and the gameplay is absolutely irredeemable.

Islets is a charming, adorable and fun little metroidvania with smooth, zippy movement, fun gimmicks and real good level design, the music is catchy, bubbly and eerie when it needs to be, definitely excited to see what the Thompson brothers can do next! If its DLC or a sequel, or something entirely new, definitely a team to look forward to from.

The length is perfect, doesn't last too long and isn't too short, just the right amount of length for a metroidvania of this size and one a few others should learn from, definitely worth the £15-£16.

This game is nothing short of life-changing. This game both cured my depression, and raised my grandfather from the dead to see me again. And when he came back and saw me playing Clownfield 2042, he wept tears of joy, not over me, but over Clownfield 2042. Clownfield 2042 is a summary of what it means to be human, and is the most beautiful game to ever grace this earth. This game is the creation of God, his will is for you to play it.
